--- title: Tasks description: Create, assign, and manage tasks with rich fields, priorities, relations, and subtasks. --- --- title: "Tasks" description: "Create, assign, and manage tasks with rich fields, priorities, relations, and subtasks." --- # Tasks A task represents a unit of work that can be assigned, progressed, and tracked. It supports rich fields, priority levels, relationships, and subtasks. ## My Tasks **My Tasks** is your personal task list across boards. By default it shows tasks assigned to you. The list groups by due time: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays at the top. Use **Group** to switch back to board groups. Saved My Tasks views remember the choice. One row of tabs sits on top, your saved views. Use **Scope** to narrow the list to some boards, and **Group: Board** to see one section per board with its count. ### Scope in My Tasks Improvement The **Scope** button in My Tasks and the standard **Scope** command in Ctrl+K now open the same board picker list. The panel has been redesigned to match the board picker you use throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for quick filtering and selection. The previous, custom implementation has been replaced with the consistent board picker experience. ### Bulk selection and actions on My Tasks You can select multiple tasks in the **My Tasks** view using the keyboard shortcut **G**, followed by **M**, to enter multi-select mode. This mirrors the selection behavior from the Kanban board for a consistent workflow. Once in multi-select mode: - **Verify your selection**: Each task you want to act on is checked. If viewing a filtered list, only tasks that are both checked and visible are included in the action. - **Apply bulk actions**: The following actions are available at the bottom of the list: - Archive - Assign - Label - Move to column - Delete - **Unselect**: Press **G** again or press **U** to exit multi-select mode. Selected rows persist until you commit an action, so you can review the working set before bulk-actioning multiple tasks. > **Tip**: The selection model matches the way you select tasks in Kanban, so if you are comfortable bulk-archiving or moving tasks on a board, the pattern transfers directly to My Tasks. ### Tasks you're snoozed on To temporarily hide tasks from your My Tasks view, set a **snooze**. When you snooze until a date: - The task no longer appears in My Tasks until that date passes - The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views. ### Saved views You can create and manage saved views on My Tasks to customize what you see. These views support: - **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more. Filter options match the Kanban board filter menu, so you can use familiar screen-level controls directly on My Tasks. - **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key. - **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards. - **Done columns hidden by default**: Done columns are hidden within each view to focus on active work. Saved views persist at the account level and can be used as templates for board filter setups. ### How it works When you toggle a filter, sort order, or board, your selection is saved with the view. The next time you open that view, the settings are applied automatically. You can create multiple views for example, one for active prioritized tasks, one for a specific project, or any combination that matches your workflow. To create a saved view, open My Tasks and use the view toolbar to pick filters and sorting options, then select **Save view**. The view appears in the saved views list alongside system views like **Involvement** and **All tasks**. ### Excluding tasks you don't need To hide distracting or temporary tasks: - Use **View filters** to show or hide assignments, priorities, or tags that don't match your current focus. - Create and pin a custom view with the exact criteria you want to see. - Review tasks by tag or priority and archive or move them away when no longer relevant. > **Note:** Saved views are scoped to the current team. Cross-board filters and sorting are supported, so you can see, for example, all high-priority inbox tasks across all boards in a single custom view. ### All Tasks view The **All Tasks** view provides an at-a-glance overview of every active task across the board. It builds split views for each board section (To Do, In Progress, Done, etc.) from a single source of truth. To access this view, navigate to the board and select **All Tasks** from the view toolbar. ### How All Tasks works All Tasks uses a single fetch pass that loads rows once and builds board splits from those rows. As a result: - Each board sees its own split of the task list. - Quiet boards do not lose splits in favor of busy boards. - The view is stable and deterministic across sessions. ### Drawing from multiple streams Since All Tasks is board-wide, it aggregates tasks from all active columns and sections, making it useful for a quick health check or high-level tracking when you need to see everything that matters—not just what's pinned or currently in one section. **Note:** Unlike **My Tasks** saved views, All Tasks does not automatically filter out onboarding, demo, template, and staging content, so those tasks may appear in the list. For visibility filtering, see [Board & Subtask Visibility](/features/board-visibility/). ### Search filters When searching within a board or in saved views, you can now narrow results using search operators on fields: - **from:** Restrict to tasks created by a specific user. - **assignee:** Restrict to tasks assigned to a specific person. - **in:** Restrict to tasks in a board, section, or column. - **label:** Restrict to tasks with a specific label. - **is:** Narrow by task type; for example, `is:card` to show only standard cards. - **dates:** Show tasks with dates matching a condition (by default, **by due**), or filter by due date ranges. - `dates:2026-09-30` For tasks with that exact due date. - `dates:<2026-09-30` For tasks due before. - `dates:>2026-09-30` For tasks due after. - `dates:in-range 2026-09-01..2026-09-30` For tasks due within the range. - `dates:overdue` For tasks marked overdue. - `dates:today` For tasks due today. - `dates:this-week` For tasks due within the current week. - `dates:later` For tasks due later than the current week. - `dates:todays` For tasks due on today and the day prior. - **has:** Show tasks that have a value in a field; for example, `has:due-date` for tasks that have a due date (including empty values) or `has:assignee` for tasks that have someone assigned. - Combining multiple operators is supported—for example, `from:alice label:urgent dates:>2026-09-30` to find urgent tasks created by Alice after a certain date. To apply search filters: 1. Open **Kanban** or **Table View**. 2. On the board header (or in the saved view toolbar), select **Filter**. 3. Choose a field and an operator, then enter a value or pick from the options. 4. Repeat for additional filters to narrow the list. Search filters apply at the board level in Kanban and in saved views. The available operators depend on the board's configuration. ### Chips in the search bar New The search bar includes: - **Chips**: Select or refine filters after your search, then click to apply chips. Click the × on a chip to remove it. - @ people picker: Start typing the @ symbol to select or create people. - # board picker: Start typing # to select or create boards. ## My Tasks toolbar Behavior change The My Tasks toolbar now uses icon-only controls with tooltips for Involvement, Columns, Scope, Filters, Sort, and Group. Active controls turn blue like Kanban, and Group shows its current choice. Overdue tooltips on red counts now appear over each overdue item. The toolbar also uses the same Save view and Reset controls as Kanban board views. From the **Ctrl+K** command palette, you can still use **Save view as** to create a saved view, and **Reset view** to revert My Tasks to its default set of built-in filters. Keyboard shortcuts like **Ctrl+S** and **Ctrl+R** no longer open popovers on the board; they now open the Save view and Reset dialogs respectively. This change makes view management across My Tasks and other board views more consistent, and ensures My Tasks mirrors the primary board interface. ## Creating a task From a board or inbox, click **New task** (or use the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl+N** / Cmd+N). This opens the task creator with the following top-level sections: - **Title**: The name or headline of the work. - **Description**: Optional text explaining what to do. - **Assignees**: One or more members to get notified and held accountable. - **Sections & Columns**: Drag the task to a section or use the section picker dropdown. - **Due date**: Pick a date or use predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or relative periods. - **Priority**: Choose Low, Medium, or High. - **Estimated time**: Optionally specify hours or a low-high range if needed. Use **Write with AI** (**Ctrl+K** / Cmd+K, or the command palette) in the description area to turn a brief task idea into a fleshed-out task. ### New Task creator New The task creator window (formerly the "Compose" button) can be opened from any view with **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and is now live for everyone. The window behaves like a task creator with Search and New Task tabs, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+J tooltips, and Tab/Shift+Tab switching. It retains your old window size and grows as you type, and the New Task button is renamed to **New Task**. On desktop, click the primary **New Task** plus button in the left sidebar to open the same window. Expand the sidebar to see its label. Hover shows **Ctrl+J**, or **Cmd+J** on Mac. Mobile keeps its existing new-task button. ### Edit a task with AI New Click **Edit with AI** under a task's description to open the AI chat in the sidebar on that task. It asks "How do you want to edit this task?" and offers ready-made requests: **Rewrite in plain words**, **Shorten the title**, **Add acceptance criteria**, **Split into sub-tasks**, and **Turn the error log into steps to reproduce**. Pick one or type your own, and the chat updates the task in place. The AI button in the description and comment editor opens the same chat. On an open task, **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J still opens the New Task window. ### AI writer failure reasons Fix When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the **Ctrl+J New Task** box and the AI Task Writer now show the real failure reason instead of hiding it; your note is still saved as a task. If AI generation is not available, the text you entered appears without modification. This applies to task creation from boards, the inbox, and description editing in task details. ## Field validation Some fields are type-checked before submission. For example, the **ranking** parameter must be a string; passing a number will fail with an error. ## OAuth connection flow When Hypertask connects to a board from an external site or app, Hypertask now shows an **approve screen** first. The screen names the connector and the exact site that will receive access, letting you confirm before any access is granted. This prevents a signed-in user from inadvertently granting external sites access to their entire board without prior approval. ## Managing task details Open a task to view and edit all its fields. Unsupported columns or fields may be hidden based on your team's board configuration. ### Priorities Assign a clear priority (Low, Medium, or High) to reflect the task's importance and replacement cost. Higher priorities should be shown ahead of lower ones in lists, table view, and filters. ### Assignees - Added assignees trigger notifications to the task's assignees. If no assignee is specified, the task is unassigned. - Workers can have their own assignee field, tracked separately from human assignees. Workers appear in the Relationships section under the *Workers* relation type. ### Due dates Click a date to pick another date or remove it. The date affects due date pickers and filter views. Predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," and relative periods also persist. ### Estimated time Type hours or a low-high range for time-tracking integration. ### Section & column Drag tasks between sections to change their column. This can trigger auto-assign rules if configured. In Table view, you can also drag any row onto another section's card; the row is the drag handle, the section card is the drop target, and the change surfaces immediately in both views (Column sort must be off for this to work; on /my-tasks, rows are grouped by time or board, so dragging doesn't target a section directly). ### Description edition UX To edit the task description: - On desktop: Click or tap the description area, then edit. - Mobile: Double-tap the description to open the editor; a single tap remains in read mode. If you are the **Task Reporter** (see below), you can edit the description directly. Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. ### Task Reporter With the **Task Reporter**, anyone on the task can update the task description directly. The Task Reporter indicator visually appears alongside comment headers, making it clear who has opened the description for editing just like comments. ### Permissions - **Task Reporter** is available to any human assignee or worker on a task. The feature is not available for closed tasks. - When you open the description in edit mode, you become the **Task Reporter** for that task. - Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. This prevents concurrent edits and restores the semantic meaning of "owner of the description field". - If you close the description without saving any changes, the status clears and the next person to open it becomes the Task Reporter. This model ensures a clear ownership of the description field, similar to comment ownership, which helps teams coordinate around tasks without stepping on each other's work. Note: While you are the Task Reporter, you cannot switch to another task description edit until the current edit state closes, preserving a single active description edit at a time. ### Saved attachments - To remove an attachment, open the description in edit mode, click the attachment you want to remove, and save. Only the items you deselect will be removed; remaining attachments are preserved as one copy each. Fix A previous bug caused the wrong attachment files to be saved when removing items from a description. When you had two or more description files attached, removing one would incorrectly save a duplicate of the other file. This is now fixed so that always only one copy of each remaining attachment is saved. Fix Deleting a task no longer creates an invalid undoable state. Undo is now always possible when restoring from deletion, ensuring tasks can be fully recovered and the undo system behaves consistently. Fix Undo functionality has been consolidated under a single restoring rule. This ensures that restoring tasks after deletion behaves the same whether you use the Undo button or Ctrl+Z, with consistent behavior tracked through the board's undo history. ### Agent lease interactions When you make manual changes to a task—"moving, assigning, unassigning, archiving, or deleting"—Hypertask cancels any active agent lease on that task and persists the change. Human modifications take priority over agent tasks, but agent-versus-agent collision protection remains in place. This ensures your task updates are never blocked by an agent while you're working. ## Task detail view Open a task to see: - Header with title, status section, assignees, workers, priority, and due date. - Description area with optional attachments. - Sections: Comments, Relations, Subtasks, Times, and Pages. - Task Reporter indicator marking who can edit the description. - **Top bar** with instant navigation and actions: - ← **Back to task** — Settings-style back button for navigation. On mobile, the back control matches the app's mobile back style with normal side spacing, making it easy to tap and fully visible up to 390px wide. - **Save** — Only right-aligned action remaining in the top bar; **Delete** is now moved to the **Undo** action in the Actions section. ### Linked pull requests Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. The pull request section displays each linked PR with its status: - **Open, Merged, Closed**: Show the current status as reported by GitHub. - **Last observed**: The last-known status before the page loads. - **Fetching...**: Indicates a background refresh is in progress. Improvement Tasks with linked PRs now show any saved PR status immediately—Open, Merged, or Closed—without waiting for GitHub to respond. Queries to GitHub run in parallel in the background and update the panel once the fetch completes, keeping the page fast and responsive. If you navigate away and come back, the PR panel refreshes again to stay current. This change eliminates wait times for tasks with linked PRs and provides an instant-open experience even when GitHub fetches are slower than usual. Security Hypertask now verifies that incoming PR updates come from known GitHub accounts before accepting them. By default, this restriction applies only to board 15. Except for board 15, an updated PR can link to any public repository, and the update is accepted as long as it originates from a trusted GitHub account. For board 15, only PR updates from three specified accounts are permitted: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team. This prevents unauthorized actors from creating, moving, or commenting on tasks in board 15 via external PRs. ### Comments The comment thread shows all comments on the task. By default, when you open a task with comments, the newest comment remains expanded so you can see the latest conversation. Link handling Plain web addresses in ticket descriptions and comments (http:// or https://) are automatically transformed into clickable links. Detects addresses based on recognized URL patterns, ensuring links in work notes and teammate discussions remain navigable on both desktop and mobile. Performance improvement When you open a task, comments now load once instead of twice. The initial SSR data used as the starting point, with React Query configured to skip a second fetch if the data is fresh. This eliminates redundant data handling and speeds up task loads: repeat visits are now approximately 0.6 seconds faster. New and edited comments still appear automatically without a reload, and realtime invalidation, reconnect reconciliation, and window-focus refresh continue to work as expected. Improvement Long task pages and comment threads now send their initial snapshot only once, reducing data copies and decoding passes. Repeat visit times drop from roughly 2.2 seconds to about 0.6 seconds. The change applies to tasks with many comments or long descriptions and focuses on the initial load speed, preserving all existing behavior for navigation, real-time updates, and comment handling. Fix The comment box on ticket pages is now positioned immediately below the last comment instead of appearing in the middle of the task. It previously moved under the task description, causing the interface to split the comment content unnaturally. The comment section now renders after other content and before the top bar, keeping comments at the bottom of the page as expected. Fix A shared comment link now opens on that comment instead of the ticket top, with the comment visible on screen on both desktop and mobile. The link scrolls directly to the referenced comment when you open it—for example, from Slack or email—making it easier to reference specific points in a conversation. This fix improves navigation for long threads with hundreds of comments and helps ticket descriptions stay readable even on narrow phones. ### Actions Common actions include: - **Back**: Navigate back to the board using the ← Back to task button. - **Move**: Relocate the task to a different section, board, or project. - **Duplicate**: Create a copy with the same fields. When duplicating a task, the new task includes the full description and can be copied to another board in one step (see board-level Duplicate in the [Boards & Sections](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/boards/) docs). - **Archive**: Hide the task from current views while keeping it in the archive. - **Delete**: Permanently remove the task. Undo appears on the notification after deletion, clicking **Undo** restores the task to its previous column and keeps it available for future edits. For bulk deletions, undo restores all affected tasks together and still works with Ctrl / Cmd+Z. Fix Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches. Fix On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth. Security Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. Board 15 now accepts automatic PR updates only from three known GitHub accounts: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team, preventing outsiders from creating tasks, moving them to review, or commenting via PRs. Security A person who is not on a board can no longer add labels to it or modify label assignments on tasks. Outsiders now receive a Forbidden error, while board members continue to manage labels as before. Security A team-only share link no longer exposes task content to outsiders. Before, the page sent the whole task and comments to unauthenticated users who only saw blurred content. Now an outsider sees an empty page with a Sign in or Login bar and cannot see task details or comments. Security When you attempt to move or nest a task under another task on an inaccessible board, the operation is refused and nothing is saved. Hypertask validates board boundaries before allowing parent-child relationships across unrelated teams, preventing accidental exposure of foreign task titles or context. ## Relations between tasks Create relationships between tasks to surface context without leaving tasks: - **Block**: Mark a task as blocking another task. - **Blocked by**: Identify what indirectly holds a task back. - **Duplicate**: Link to other tasks that represent the same work item. - **Workers**: Associate an agent or intelligent agent with the task for scheduling and coordination. See a task's relations in the **Relations** section of the task detail view. ## Subtasks Break down a task into smaller units. Subtasks appear in the task detail under the **Subtasks** section. Mark them complete to show progress toward the parent task. Add one from the parent task's **Subtasks** section. The window lists tasks you can link as a sub-task, and the **New sub-task** button under the search box opens the normal create window with the parent already attached. Typing a name that matches nothing still creates a new sub-task when you press Enter. ## Task property rail The task detail sidebar includes a rail of properties (title, priority, assignees, labels, etc.). The rail now occupies the full remaining dynamic viewport height, so it uses all available space rather than a fixed maximum and leaves no unused viewport space. **Task properties no longer scroll with the task thread**, keeping them pinned to the sidebar for easy access while browsing comments and history. When another browser, the CLI, or an agent changes a task, its open detail page refreshes the title, assignees, labels, priority, dates, status, attachments, and linked pull requests without a reload. If the live connection is unavailable, the page checks for changes every 10 seconds. ## Time tracking Track work hours on tasks via the **Times** section: - **B** opens the time entry modal from the task, or use the command palette ("Log time"). - Manual per-day rows let you log time for any calendar day without a timer. - Export time logs as CSV for payroll or reporting. See the [Time Tracking](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/) guide for full details. ## AI Task Writer The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs. ### How it works today The Task Writer writes tasks in your team's style. It uses board-aware prompts, pulls task templates from boards, and uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them. ### Using the Task Writer - From a board: **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and select **Create with AI** — **Task Writer**. - From the command palette: **Ctrl+K** — search for "Task Write" and select it. - From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select **Task Writer**. After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description. ### Board task templates Save a representative ticket through **Ctrl+K → Save as template**. Open **Settings → Board → Task templates** to edit its name, title pattern, and description structure. Use names such as **Bug** or **A/B test** so the writer can match your request to the right template. Simple descriptions support headings written with `##` and plain paragraphs. Rich descriptions remain read-only here to preserve their formatting; you can still change their names and title patterns. If someone else saves first, reload before saving your changes. When you explicitly request ideas, the writer fills them in one pass using board tickets, documents, memory, and custom instructions. For example, “Write an A/B test with five headlines” produces five finished headlines, not placeholders. A matched template's title pattern and headings stay in place. Required ICE scores include the component scores and mark estimates. Ordinary editing requests still preserve your source instead of inventing copy. ## Instant ticket opening New Tickets now load instantly from cached board data, with no spinner, no "Loading..." text, and no placeholder animation. The entire opening experience is fast and lag-free across desktop and mobile. ### What you see - **Click to open**: When you tap or click a task, it appears in about 0.15 to 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile. - **No loading animation**: No full-screen spinner, no pulsing grey bars, no brief placeholder state. - **Suggested questions right away**: If the AI panel is open, suggested questions appear immediately—not waiting for the API response. ### Browser history The browser back and forward buttons now behave consistently with the app: - Press **Back** to return to the board. The board remains loaded and you can stay there. - Press **Forward** to re-open the last ticket you viewed. This lets you browse through tasks inside the app while the rest of your session stays tight and fast. ### Performance details - Median open times are ~0.15 seconds on desktop and ~0.17 seconds on mobile. - The first open after a board loads takes about 0.25 to 0.33 seconds; subsequent opens are closer to 0.13 to 0.18 seconds. - The first open after a board loads now paints its cached title and description before expensive editing property controls, so the title and description appear instantly while controls like assignees, status, and priority still warm. This tighter paint-first sequence reduces the first-open delta to about 0.10 seconds—considerably faster than before. ### Visual smoothness Fix Ticket pages no longer shift or jitter after opening. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear instantly as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across desktop and mobile for all test accounts. ### Keyboard shortcuts We recommend using keyboard shortcuts to navigate: - **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J to jump to a task or open it with the Task Writer. - **Ctrl+O** / Cmd+O to jump to a task or link from within the task detail. These shortcuts preserve the instant-open feel and keep you moving without page spins or wait states. ### Assignee persistence Improvement When you assign a task from the assign picker, closing the picker or pressing Escape no longer drops the assignment. The human assignee name stays on the task and persists across page reloads and subsequent checks. This applies whether you assign from the board card or from a direct task link. ### Faster task opening Improved Pressing **Back** after opening a subtask now shows the parent task immediately instead of the subtask, with no "Loading..." flash, and **Forward** returns you to the subtask if needed. Opening a task directly from cached data shows it reliably within about 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile, eliminating previous delays. ### Navigating to previous titles in Inbox Improved Using **J** or the arrow keys to move to the next Inbox item now loads and displays it within about 0.3 seconds on desktop and mobile, removing lag that previously held up the wrong ticket title for up to several seconds. ### No flash of the ticket title after opening a board card Fixed Pressing **Back** right after opening a board card now shows the board immediately, with no flash of the ticket title. In at least 19 of 20 quick Backs (within 0.3 seconds of opening a card), you see only the board, not the ticket, and the board is visible within 1 second. ### Task detail downloads once Fix Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches. ### Board tap loading Fix On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth. ### Faster open on cold phone Improved Opening a task on a cold phone with no cached data now shows its title and description sooner (11.8 s vs 14.1 s median, 95th-percentile gap of ~2.3 s). The first load paints the title and description earlier, while controls like assignee and priority still warm up afterward, keeping the experience instant and frictionless. ### Ticket page no longer shifts on mobile Fix The ticket page no longer jumps on first load. The comment box appears once and never moves: 20 of 20 fresh loads on two test accounts, on both desktop and phone. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear immediately as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across platforms for all test accounts. ### Comments no longer jump with content Behavior change The comment box and comment thread no longer shift downward as content loads, so the task layout stays consistent across desktop and mobile from open to load. ### Instant board tap New Clicking a board card now initializes the task with a single board interaction instead of triggering redundant rendering. This keeps the opening experience snappy across desktop and mobile, especially after boards have already been reloaded. Loading address-bar updates that occur as part of the navigation are tracked correctly as navigations within the same page rather than distinct page loads. The change applies across all boards and view types—Kanban, table, and card lists—with consistent, performant behavior. ## Invited-in aspects and board validation Improved Pages that use invite links now validate board context before sending requests. **My Tasks** and **Inbox** no longer fire invite-link requests without an associated board, which previously caused console errors for unmatched requests. With this fix, such invalid requests now surface a clear, user-facing message instead of a server error, keeping the console clean and providing explicit feedback when a board context is required.

title: Gated downloads for ticket viewers only
description: Only people who can see a ticket can download its files.
---

Downloads were previously reachable for board members without proper task-level visibility because a legacy access check only validated board membership.

The system now attaches a per-ticket access gate to file download paths. A download succeeds only when a user has board membership and task visibility (i.e., can see the ticket). Observers outside the parent task regardless of broader board access receive not found or are blocked.

This change closes a gap where draft task attachments or other files could be retrieved by users who should not see that context including AI-generated previews on private tickets.

---
title: Collaboration
description: Share a board with Admins and Members. There is no Viewer role. Invite a client to one board, and see who manages billing.
---


Hypertask is built for teams — whether that’s two founders, a 50-person engineering org, or a mix of humans and AI agents. Every feature is designed around the idea that project management is inherently collaborative.

## Team workspaces
Workspaces are the top-level container in Hypertask. Each workspace groups related projects together and manages team membership.

A workspace might represent your company, a department, or a client engagement. You can belong to multiple workspaces.

## Project members
### Inviting people
Invite team members to a project by generating an **invite link**. Invite links support several controls:

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Expiration** | Set when the link stops working (e.g. 7 days, 30 days, never) |
| **Usage limit** | Cap how many people can join via this link |
| **Domain restriction** | Limit invites to specific email domains (e.g. `@yourcompany.com`) |

<aside type="tip">
Domain restrictions are useful when you want to share an invite link broadly (in Slack, for example) but limit access to people within your organization.
</aside>

### Roles and access

A board has an owner. The owner can set each other person to **Admin** or **Member**. Those are the only two roles you can assign, and the owner’s own role cannot be changed.

There is no Viewer role and no read-only role. Someone who only needs to look at a board still joins as an Admin or a Member.

Manage the people on a board in **Settings > Board > Members**. That list is for the board you have open.

To let a client see a single board, invite them to that board only. People see a board when they own it or are a member of it, so a client invited to one board does not see your other boards.

Billing is under **Settings > Team > Billing**. The team owner can view billing and update the payment method. The team owner, the board owner, or a board Admin can view billing details and change the billing email.

### BYOK and API keys
API key management is available to **BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)** teams. BYOK teams see and manage API keys directly in the **Settings → Team** navigation. For non-BYOK teams, the API Keys entry is hidden from this section.

## AI Agents
AI agents can be added to boards just like human team members. When you add an agent to a board, it gains access to that board’s tasks and can be assigned work, @mentioned in comments, and participate in the project workflow.

### Adding agents to boards
<Steps>
1. Open the board’s settings or invite panel.
2. Look for the **invite modal** — it shows both team members and any agents you’ve created.
3. Select the agent you want to add to the board.
4. The agent appears in the board’s member list and can be assigned tasks.
</Steps>

Agents added to a board are treated as members of that board. This means:
- Agents appear in the assignee dropdown for tasks on that board
- Agents can be @mentioned in comments and will receive notifications
- Agents can read and update tasks on that board via MCP

<aside type="note">
Agents do not count as team seats toward your subscription limit. You can add as many agents as you need without affecting your seat count.
</aside>

### Agent access scope
When you create an agent, it inherits access to all boards in projects where you’re a member. Use the board-level invite modal to **restrict which boards an agent can access** — boards not on the list treat the agent as if it doesn’t exist.

This is useful when:
- You work across multiple clients or teams and don’t want a given agent active everywhere
- You want to limit an agent to only the boards where it has relevant context
- You have specialized agents for different workflows and need to keep them scoped

## Feedback
Give feedback directly from the app with a prominent call-to-action. The feedback button is always available at the bottom of the app shell rail and opens a fully-featured real feedback modal with:
- Fast-track submission fields for quick suggestions
- Rich text support so you can include screenshots, drafts, or detailed feature requests
- Clear category selection to route your feedback to the right teams
- Direct posting to the Feedback board with auto-assignment

<aside type="tip">
Use the feedback button to share ideas, report bugs, or suggest improvements. Your input shapes future releases and directly affects the UX improvements we ship.
</aside>

## @mentions
Type `@` in any comment to mention a team member. Mentions do two things:
1. **Send a notification** — the mentioned person receives an inbox notification immediately.
2. **Add as follower** — the mentioned person is automatically added as a follower on the task, so they receive future updates.

Mentions work in comments and task descriptions, and support native and external agents:

<aside type="tip">
If you receive a mention that looks suspicious, report it to your workspace owner.
</aside>

### Agent @mentions
<aside type="note">
Agent owners are not notified of their own agent’s comments.
</aside>
@mentioning an agent (native or external) triggers a **Mentioned notification** in that agent’s inbox. External agents with scoped tokens receive notifications via their `agent_notifications` array and can poll it with `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "list"`) to pick up mentions.

This means you can @mention external agents in comments and task descriptions to trigger automation; the agent’s inbox receives a Mentioned notification, and it can respond via MCP comments with proper HTML markup.

If an external agent isn’t receiving @mentions, verify that it has board-level access.

## Emoji reactions
React to tasks and comments with emoji. Reactions serve as lightweight feedback — a quick thumbs-up to acknowledge work, a flag to signal concern, or a celebration when something ships.

### Fast like button
For the most common reaction — a simple thumbs-up — Hypertask provides a **fast like button** that appears directly on task cards and comment rows. No need to open the full emoji picker:

- **Mouse users:** hover over a task card or comment row to reveal the like button, which shows a tooltip with a "[L]" hint; click it to toggle your reaction on or off.
- **Mobile users:** tap the like button that appears inline alongside the comment or task actions.

The like button is a shortcut for the thumbs-up reaction. It appears in the full reactions list alongside any other emoji your teammates have added, and it triggers the same notification to the author as any other reaction.

### Mobile emoji picker
On mobile devices, emoji reactions are organized into a docked picker that mimics popular messaging apps:
- Picker appears docked at the bottom of the screen, aligned with the keyboard input area
- A search bar on the Emoji tab lets you quickly find emojis by name
- Selecting an emoji immediately applies it as a reaction, with the picker closing automatically

### Comment display
Comments can be starred (saved) or pinned, and the visual indicators update based on comment state:
1. **Pinned + saved** — only the orange pinned dot displays (saved state is suppressed)
2. **Pinned only** — only the orange pinned dot displays
3. **Saved only** — only the yellow saved/starred dot displays

### All reactions icon
Click the activity icon next to a comment to see all reactions. This icon appears when someone has reacted in any way, whether it’s a like or another emoji expression.

## Agent decision requests
Agents can ask you for decisive feedback on tickets. When an agent encounters a decision that impacts work (e.g., "Archive this task," "Move to inactive," etc.), it opens a **decision request** on the ticket with one-tap approve/answer buttons.

### Triggering decision requests
Decision requests appear as inline panels on the ticket:
- **Approve** — Applies the agent’s suggested action with one tap
- **Reject / More options** — Opens a menu with detailed choices or alternative actions

Agents only create decision requests when the suggested action clearly affects board state and benefits from human sign-off. Routine summaries, AI editor outputs, and informational messages do not trigger requests.

### Agent aftermath
Once you respond:
- **Approved decisions** — The agent applies the action to the ticket immediately (e.g., archives the task and adds a reason comment)
- **Rejected or alternative** — The agent stops iterating on that item and moves on, leaving the ticket in its current state

You can review all pending decision requests anytime in the ticket feed — the panel stays visible until resolved.

## Real-time sync
Hypertask keeps every connected client live — no manual refreshes needed. Changes made anywhere in the app (or via the CLI and MCP) appear instantly for everyone who has the same board open.

**What updates in real time:**
- Tasks appearing, disappearing, or moving between sections when created, archived, or moved
- Task title, status, priority, and assignee changes
- New comments and reactions
- Board and section changes

Creating a task from the CLI and watching it appear on an open board with no page reload is a first-class workflow — useful for monitoring agents running in your terminal or CI pipeline.

### Real-time collaborative text editing
Multiple people can edit the same rich-text field at the same time, with changes merged automatically.

This applies to:
- Task descriptions
- Comments (while drafting)
- Any rich text field in the app

There are no save buttons — changes persist as you type.

<aside>
Real-time sync means AI agents editing task descriptions via MCP won’t overwrite human edits. Changes are merged automatically.
</aside>

## Managing comments
You can manage comments on any task — including comments left by other team members or agents. This is useful when:
- Cleaning up outdated or irrelevant comments
- Removing agent-generated comments that are no longer needed
- Tidying up task threads for better readability

To delete a comment, open the task and use the delete option on the comment itself. Comment management is available to all project members — trust within the team is assumed for collaborative housekeeping.

### Comment hover panel
The comment hover panel in table views and card lists is streamlined for faster access to actions:
- **Reply** — standard reply action
- **React** — add or remove a reaction (thumbs-up, favorite, flag, etc.)
- **Three-dot menu** — click the three-dot to reveal remaining options

Press and hold <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (or the three-dot itself) to access the full menu with all comment commands pinned at the top:
- **Edit** — modify the comment
- **Summarize** — generate an AI summary of the comment thread
- **Fast like** — quickly add a thumbs-up reaction

For the most common reaction, just hover and click the like button directly on the comment row. No need to open the full emoji picker.

### Mobile long press to actions
On a phone, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with that comment's actions at the top. **Edit comment** is first when you wrote the comment. Swiping a comment is off so it does not fight the task swipe that already moves you to the next or previous ticket.

### Mobile comment actions menu
When you open a comment's Command Center on mobile, the first actions are the comment ones:
- **Edit**: open the comment composer (shown first when you wrote the comment)
- **Delete**: remove the comment from the thread
- **Star or turn off star**: save or unsave the comment
- **Pin or turn off pin**: pin the comment to the top of the feed

### URL auto-linkification
Bare URLs in comments are automatically converted into clickable links at render time, regardless of how the comment was created. This applies to comments posted via the web UI, CLI, MCP, or any API client — so a deploy URL pasted by a CLI script or an agent's status update with a link will always be clickable for your teammates.

Links open in a new tab. URLs that are already formatted as hyperlinks or embedded inside images are left unchanged.

### Quoted replies
When you reply to a comment, Hypertask inserts a placeholder for the quoted message.

### GIFs and emoji in comments
The comment composer includes a built-in **Emoji & GIFs picker** with two tabs, giving you Slack-style expressiveness in task discussions.

#### Slash commands
Type a slash command at the start of your comment to open the picker instantly:

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `/emoji` | Opens the picker on the **Emoji** tab |
| `/giphy` | Opens the picker on the **GIFs** tab |

#### Emoji tab
Browse and search a full emoji library. Click any emoji to insert it into your comment at the cursor position.

#### GIFs tab
The GIFs tab is powered by **Giphy** and offers two modes:
- **Trending** — shows popular GIFs by default when you open the tab.
- **Search** — type any query to find a GIF that fits the moment.

Click a GIF to insert it into your comment. Inserted GIFs render as **resizable media** — drag the corner handles to adjust the size, and the chosen dimensions are preserved when the comment is posted.

<aside type="note">
GIF search requires a Giphy API key configured on the Hypertask deployment. If GIFs are not loading, contact your workspace admin.
</aside>

## Comment edit mode
Edit a comment to refine your thoughts or fix mistakes. The editor includes keyboard shortcuts to help you work efficiently:

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **ESC** | Leave edit mode without sending (clears unsaved edits) |
| **Ctrl+Enter** | Send the edited comment |

### Exiting edit mode
When you’re in edit mode and want to abandon your changes:
- **Mouse:** click the trash can icon in the edit-mode footer
- **Keyboard:** press **ESC**

Both options exit edit mode without posting the comment and without polluting the conversation with draft text.

## Activity logs
Every change in Hypertask is recorded in the activity log — a full audit trail of who did what, and when.

Tracked actions include:
- Task creation, updates, and deletion
- Section moves
- Assignment and priority changes
- Comments and reactions
- Member joins and leaves
- Board and section modifications

Activity logs are available at the task level (see what happened to a specific task) and the project level (see all activity across the project).

### Comments-only view (default)
The task feed defaults to **comments only** — history events such as field changes, assignments, and status moves are hidden to reduce noise. This keeps the conversation readable at a glance, especially on busy tickets.

To reveal history events:
- Click the **Show history** pill at the top of the feed, or
- Press **`Ctrl+Shift+H`**

Both controls toggle history events on and off. You can also access **Show/Hide history** and **Expand/Collapse all comments** from the command palette (`Ctrl+K`).

<aside type="tip">
If you need a full audit trail of every change on a task, use **Show history** (`Ctrl+Shift+H`) to surface all activity events inline with the comment thread.
</aside>

--- title: MCP Integration description: Connect AI agents to Hypertask via the Model Context Protocol. --- Hypertask provides a full [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP) server that lets AI agents create, update, search, and manage tasks programmatically. Any MCP-compatible client can connect to Hypertask and operate as an autonomous worker. Setting up a new agent? See [Connect a new agent](/connect-an-agent/). ## What is MCP? The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that defines how AI models interact with external tools and data sources. Instead of building custom integrations for each AI client, Hypertask exposes a single MCP server that works with all of them. MCP uses a tool-based architecture: the server advertises available operations (list tasks, create task, add comment, etc.) and the AI client calls them as needed to complete user requests. ## Transport Connect with Streamable HTTP at: ```text https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp ``` Send your bearer token on every request. The server handles each JSON-RPC request independently and does not create a server-side session. It does not require a session ID and ignores one if your client sends it. Use POST for MCP calls. Responses are JSON, or an SSE-formatted response when the client requests only `text/event-stream`. There is no persistent stream at this endpoint. Authenticated GET and DELETE requests return **405 Method Not Allowed**. ### Older clients Clients that only support the older SSE transport can connect to `https://mcp.hypertask.ai/sse`. That connection creates a session. The client sends messages to the `/message?sessionId=...` address supplied by the stream. Both requests need the bearer token. ### Tool discovery The server lists tools grouped by resource, such as projects, tasks, and reports. Each tool has an `action` and an `input` object for that action's fields. Use the names and schemas returned by your client's tool list. The available actions depend on your token's permissions. When an MCP client writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link, the image appears inline by default. Ask for "attachment only" or "link only", or set `inline_images` to `false`, to keep it as an attachment or link instead. Uploading images to someone else's comment adds attachments without changing their text. ## AI Assistant Self-Onboarding Memorystore apps and public marketing pages on hypertask.ai can automatically discover the MCP server address by opening the `llms.txt` file: ``` https://hypertask.ai/llms.txt https://app.hypertask.ai/llms.txt https://mcp.hypertask.ai/llms.txt ``` The file returns a human-readable instructions block that includes: - **Connect-An-AI-Assistant block** with instructions and steps for Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, and CLI environments - **MCP endpoint URL** (`https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`) for direct connection - Authentication instructions using JWT bearer tokens This enables AI assistants to self-discover and connect to Hypertask without manual configuration. For environments that support `llms.txt` parsing (such as Claude Desktop and ChatGPT's current and future releases), the protocol automatically applies the connection details. ### Authentication MCP connections are authenticated with **JWT bearer tokens**. To get your personal API key: 1. Open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) and sign in. 2. Go to **Settings** (gear icon in the sidebar), then **Connect**, then **MCP**. 3. Copy your personal API key (**Generate** or **Renew**, then **Copy**).
You can also reach the MCP token dialog directly from the command palette: press Ctrl+K and search for **MCP**. The dialog includes a shortcut to the CLI install dialog if you want to set up the terminal CLI at the same time.
A token you generate on this screen expires after **30 days**. Renew it here and paste the new value into the client. A connection you approve in the browser lasts **90 days**. If the client is refused, see [MCP troubleshooting](/mcp/troubleshooting/).
## Authenticated unknown paths All unrecognized paths under `/api/mcp/*` now require authentication. Previously, unknown paths (such as `/api/mcp/unknown/path`) returned 404 even for authenticated requests, which could leak information during route enumeration. They now consistently return appropriate auth errors (401) when called without valid credentials. This is reflected in the MCP tools reference under appropriate endpoints (e.g., creation/UPDATE operations where path is implied), and in the REST API documentation at `/api/rest-api.mdx`. ## Agent bearer tokens When an autonomous agent authenticates with its own bearer token (distinct from a human user's token), all write operations - task creation, comment posting, assignments - are attributed to the agent itself, not to the agent's owner. This means activity logs, notifications, and task histories correctly reflect the agent as the actor, making it straightforward to audit which agent made which change. **Person tokens work for agent creation**: When you create an agent through MCP and authenticate with a person token (your own API key), the server now validates the authentication and returns an agent in addition to the usual service account agent response. Previously, using a person token resulted in "Authentication failed". Now, a person token can create an agent, and the connection details are returned so the new agent can be set up using its own token or managed through the CLI. ## Agent identity You can manage agents as service accounts with scoped API keys. Configure agents to: - Create and rotate API keys via MCP - Restrict keys with project-level and model-level scopes - Display a bot badge in UI and in MCP tool metadata This makes each agent behave like a dedicated account with its own permission profile. Agents can be created, updated, or deactivated via MCP, and their scoped keys are scoped to the scopes they were assigned. ## Expose board AI custom instructions over MCP In addition to skills and playbooks, you can manage board AI custom instructions directly from MCP: - **GET `/api/mcp/projects/[projectId]/instructions`** - Retrieve the currently configured board-level custom instructions. - **PUT `/api/mcp/projects/[projectId]/instructions`** - Update or reset the board AI custom instructions. This complements the MCP-exposed skills and playbooks, giving agents full control over board-level AI behavior without needing to navigate to the UI. ## Provide agent lease heartbeats Agents can safely claim, heartbeat, and release tasks via dedicated endpoints under `/api/mcp/tasks/lease/`: - **POST `/api/mcp/tasks/lease/claim`** - Claim an available task for handling. - **POST `/api/mcp/tasks/lease/heartbeat`** - Broadcast ongoing work (heartbeats) to keep the lease alive. - **POST `/api/mcp/tasks/lease/release`** - Release a claimed task so others can pick it up. These endpoints allow agents to coordinate worker pools without races, supporting multi-agent workflows and shared task queues. ## Re-enabling external agents mint fresh MCP credentials When you turn an agent back on, Hypertask mint a fresh MCP credential for it if the agent has none: - The API returns `hasMcpToken`: true for an active external agent in agent detail responses, and shows no raw `mcpToken` field. - A copyable configuration is shown once so the UI cannot claim an unusable agent is active. - Old credentials remain revoked; new credentials are used for authenticating via MCP. - Owners-only agents and external agents both receive this behavior, ensuring credentials are always available on re-enable. ## Move tasks to inbox via MCP You can now trigger tasks to move to your inbox programmatically: - **Move task to inbox** - Takes a task identifier (ID or uniqueIndex) and marks the task as unread, clearing any existing folder, adding it to the Inbox section, and resetting the priority to high. - Available via MCP tools and the CLI, enabling agents and workflows to reactively route high-priority work into your inbox. ## Agent-tier rate limits Authenticated agent tokens that carry valid `htk_` API keys receive a higher rate-limit tier: - **Base:** 120 requests/minute for unauthenticated or invalid keys - **Agent-tier:** 600 requests/minute for authenticated agents with valid `htk_` keys This mode specifically applies to agent traffic; non-agent traffic remains subject to the base limits. Agent-tier tokens are detected via the `Authorization` header that must include a valid Hypertask API key. ## Creating agents with your own token You can create an agent using your own bearer token when it has the required permissions. Configure that token in your MCP client. You do not need a separate browser session for MCP calls. ## Full capability parity across surfaces The MCP server now exposes 81 of 96 core capabilities across the API, CLI, AI Chat, and HyperAI. New and extended tools match REST endpoint behavior for board configuration, project administration, profile updates, page history, task description history, and relations composition. All tools are thin wrappers over the same REST routes that power the web UI, ensuring consistent behavior regardless of which surface you use. We also measure that claim. The agents dashboard can show a weekly MCP-versus-CLI eval for Claude, Cursor, and Codex. See Agents Dashboard. ## Client configuration Add to your Claude Desktop config file (`claude_desktop_config.json`). Use your personal API key from Hypertask: **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** → copy API key. ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertasks": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` Add to your project's `.mcp.json` or global `~/.claude/mcp.json`, or run `claude mcp add --transport http hypertask https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`. Use your personal API key from Hypertask: **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** → copy API key. ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertasks": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` Open **Settings > MCP Servers** and add a new server. Use your personal API key from Hypertask: **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** → copy API key. ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertasks": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P) and run **MCP: Open User Configuration**, or add this to `.vscode/mcp.json`. Requires VS Code 1.99 or later. Use your personal API key from Hypertask: **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** → copy API key. ```json { "servers": { "hypertask-mcp": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` 1. Open **Settings > Connectors > Personal connectors > New MCP server**. 2. Enter `https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`. 3. Choose **Bearer token** and paste your personal API key from Hypertask **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** (**Generate** or **Renew**, then **Copy**). Requires a paid Lovable plan. Hypertask exposes an **OpenAPI schema** that ChatGPT can consume as a custom action or GPT integration. This lets ChatGPT create tasks, list projects, search tickets, and more - without needing native MCP support. 1. In ChatGPT, open **My GPTs** (or the GPT editor for a custom GPT you control). 2. Go to **Actions - Add action**. 3. Import the Hypertask OpenAPI schema from: ``` https://mcp.hypertask.ai/openapi.json ``` 4. Under **Authentication**, choose **API Key** and paste your personal API key from **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP**. Set the header name to `Authorization` and the value format to `Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. 5. Save the action. ChatGPT will now list the available Hypertask operations and can call them on your behalf.
The OpenAPI schema is auto-generated from the same endpoints that power the MCP server, so it always stays in sync with the latest tools. Any new MCP tool automatically appears as an available action in ChatGPT.
## AI Chat integration AI Chat exposes equivalents for most MCP operations and shares the same assignment behavior layer. Its tool definitions are maintained separately, so each new MCP parameter still needs an AI Chat adapter when the input shape differs. AI Chat reads and writes, and it is not a reduced version of MCP. It manages tasks, comments, drafts, pages, labels, views, skills, sections, timers and task relations, assigns people or board agents, moves tasks between boards and to the inbox, reads board manifests and playbooks, checks agent presence, and raises decision requests. Its task-update operation is the richest of any surface: it alone adds or removes a single label without replacing the rest, and writes to several tasks in one call. For assignment and unassignment, AI Chat accepts a person's user ID, `me`, display name, or email. It also accepts a board agent's display name or UUID. Agent matching is case-insensitive and board-scoped; a person-agent name collision returns an explicit ambiguity error. Two MCP operations have no AI Chat equivalent, and neither is a capability gap: the `hello` action of `hypertask_user_context` (the connection-time onboarding map, which the chat gets from its system prompt) and the `report` action of `hypertask_time`. Some capabilities are shared but named differently. MCP folds comment edits into `hypertask_comments` (`action: "update"`), unassign into `hypertask_tasks` (`action: "assign"`), and every timer action into `hypertask_time`, where AI Chat gives each its own tool. AI Chat also has three tools no other surface has: `search_help_docs`, `rag_retrieval` over indexed board content, and `web_search`. ## Known limitations | Feature | Status | Details | |---------|--------|---------| | **@mentions in comments** | Partial | The `mentions` parameter on `hypertask_comments` (`action: "add"`) works, but mentions can render as plain text without firing a notification. Pass structured mention objects (`user_id` + `display_name`) for reliable results. | | **Auto-linking ticket references** | Not supported | A ticket reference inside a comment posted over MCP is not turned into a related-task link the way the web UI does it. Call `hypertask_tasks` (`action: "link"`) to create the relation explicitly. | | **Pages and description history** | Supported | Version listing and restore for pages and task descriptions exist at `/api/mcp/pages/versions`, `/pages/restore`, `/tasks/description-versions` and `/tasks/description-restore`, and are exposed by the `versions` and `restore` actions on `hypertask_pages` and `hypertask_tasks`. | | **Agent infrastructure** | REST only, by design | Task leases, evidence, escalation, work sessions, service-account management, and API keys are REST endpoints only. Webhooks are exposed by `hypertask_webhooks`. They are plumbing for autonomous workers rather than things an assistant should call mid-conversation. |
Creating labels and managing saved views used to be listed here as unsupported. Both work now, from every surface: `hypertask_labels` (`action: "create"`), and the `create`, `update`, `delete` and `switch` actions of `hypertask_views`.
## Troubleshooting Expired API keys, a 30-day token from Settings, a 90-day approved connection, and a connection that stops on **Approve and connect** are covered in [MCP troubleshooting](/mcp/troubleshooting/). **"Failed to Connect to MCP"** — If the credential is still current and the client cannot connect: 1. Confirm the URL is exactly `https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp` (including `/mcp`). Older clients can still use `https://mcp.hypertask.ai/sse`. 2. Check that the `Authorization` header is formatted as `Bearer ` with a space after "Bearer". 3. Restart your MCP client after updating the configuration. **"No tools listed after MCP sign-in"** - If you signed in successfully but the last step doesn't show tools: 1. Verify you're using the correct MCP server addresses for your client. The primary address is `https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`. Some clients have additional endpoints for meta-only loading: `https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`. 2. Check that your token has permission to use the actions you need. 3. Ensure the client is configured to wait for the tool list. Some clients proceed immediately and skip displaying available tools. **"Authentication failed" when creating an agent with your token** - Check the bearer token in your MCP client configuration and confirm it has permission to create agents. A browser sign-in does not replace the token on MCP requests. **Unknown input field** — Remove the unsupported field. A nearby spelling may suggest the accepted name. For example, `contnet` in a comment suggests `text`. Use the suggestion, then retry the request. Unrelated names receive no guess. Suggestions never change which fields are accepted. ## Supported clients Hypertask MCP works with any client that supports the MCP standard, and ChatGPT via the OpenAPI adapter: - **Claude Code** - Anthropic's CLI agent - **Claude Desktop** - Anthropic's desktop app - **Cursor** - AI-powered code editor - **VS Code** - 1.99 or later, via **MCP: Open User Configuration** or `.vscode/mcp.json` - **Windsurf** - Codeium's AI editor - **ChatGPT** - via the Hypertask OpenAPI schema (custom actions / GPTs) - **Lovable** - personal connectors on a paid plan, with a bearer token - **Any MCP-compatible agent** - anything that speaks the protocol ## Next steps

--- title: Creating Agents description: Create and manage autonomous AI agents in Hypertask, connect them via MCP, and assign them tasks on your board. --- This guide covers the complete agent onboarding flow in Hypertask â\x80\x94 from creating your first agent to adding it to your Kanban board where it can be assigned tasks, mentioned in comments, and controlled via MCP clients or agentic CLIs. ## Overview Agents in Hypertask act as autonomous team members. They have their own identity, can be assigned tasks, receive notifications, and interact with the board using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or the Hypertask CLI. ## Creating an agent See [Connect a new agent](/connect-an-agent/) for the complete setup. 1. **Create an agent.** Choose one path: - **Agent Chat:** Open [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat), choose **+ Add agent**, enter a name, and choose **Create**. The agent starts with no boards. Copy the token shown once before choosing **Done**. - **From a board:** Open a team board and use **Ctrl+K > Create agent**. Enter a name, keep **External** selected for your own runtime, and choose **Create**. This attaches the agent to that board and opens its page. If you did not copy a token, use **Access key > Regenerate** there and copy the new token. 2. **Add boards.** The person who owns the agent opens [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents), opens the agent, expands **Board access**, and ticks each board they want it to use. Changes save immediately. Turn the agent on first if disabled. **Board settings > Agents** only lists agents already attached to that board. It has no add control. Private agents are visible only to their owner. An agent can only join boards in its team; the first board establishes that team.
An agent cannot add itself to a board, whatever its role. Admin agents can add other agents of the same owner only on boards they already belong to. Promoting an agent to admin is not an onboarding fix; its owner must grant access first.
## Managing agents Open [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents) and select your agent to manage its **Board access** and **Access key**. Use **Regenerate** to replace a lost token or **Revoke** to remove it. ### Monitoring agent work Open an agent from the Agents page to see what its worker is doing now. The detail page shows: - **Working now:** The active ticket, elapsed time, runtime, model, heartbeat, and latest progress. - **Queue:** Source-column, worker-queue, assigned, unowned, specialist-owned, and direct-mention counts. - **Up next:** The worker's actual ticket order. Desktop shows the next three tickets; mobile shows the next two. - **Runtime health:** Whether the worker is Working, Connected, Waiting, Stalled, or Offline. - **Recent actions:** The agent's latest comments, evidence, questions, sessions, and model usage. Live worker data is labeled **Live worker**. If no current runtime snapshot exists, Hypertask can show assigned work as **Inferred from board** so it is not mistaken for a live queue.
The enabled switch and runtime health answer different questions. An agent can be enabled while its worker is offline. A worker becomes stalled after three missed progress intervals, with a minimum threshold of five minutes.
## Connecting an agent Hypertask agents support two connection methods: **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** for direct client integration, and the **Hypertask CLI** for terminal-based and scripted workflows. Both methods use a bearer token issued per agent. The access key is for a managed agent's own identity, and connecting your own editor (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code) uses your personal API key from **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** instead ([Authentication](/mcp/overview/#authentication)). ### Retrieving the agent token 1. Open [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents) and open the agent you own. 2. Find **Access key**. If you no longer have the token, choose **Regenerate**. 3. Copy the new token and store it securely. Use it in the connection examples below.
Regenerating a token invalidates the previous one. Tokens have no expiry but can be revoked or replaced.
### Connection methods Paste the entire configuration snippet into your AI tool (e.g., Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Claude Code). ```json { "mcpServers": { "hypertask-agent": { "type": "sse", "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/sse", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_AGENT_TOKEN" } } } } ``` Some tools only require the URL and bearer token. Use the agent's token in the `Authorization` header: ```bash hypertask --token YOUR_AGENT_TOKEN task list ``` ### Add a board with the owner's login Use the owner's own login, not the agent token or an agent-bound connection: ```bash hypertask agents update --id --add-project ``` Invitations through the CLI or MCP need the agent UUID, not its display name. See the [CLI commands](/cli/commands/#hypertask-agents-update). ### Using a management key With permissioned management keys, you can create agents, change their board memberships, and manage their tokens from the CLI: ```bash # Create a new agent on one or more boards hypertask agents create --name "Reviewer Bot" \ --project \ --management-key CONTROLLER_KEY # Add or remove boards from an existing agent. Both project flags are repeatable. hypertask agents update --id AGENT_ID \ --add-project \ --remove-project \ --management-key CONTROLLER_KEY # Rotate or revoke the agent token hypertask agents rotate-token --id AGENT_ID --management-key CONTROLLER_KEY hypertask agents revoke --id AGENT_ID --management-key CONTROLLER_KEY ``` Management keys allow controlled, external authorization flows (e.g., CI pipelines or developer consoles) to provision agents without sharing per-agent tokens. #### Limit a management key to one team Team-scoped management keys are available during the Owner + QA rollout. Open **Settings > Management keys**, create a key, and choose a team instead of **Whole account**. The generated key starts with httk_; existing account-wide keys continue to start with htmk_. A team-scoped management key can: - List and manage only agents whose boards all belong to the selected team. - Create agents only when at least one selected board belongs to that team. - Read AI usage only for the selected team when you own it. - Create or revoke other management keys only within the same team. It cannot use account-wide token, connection, gateway-key, or data routes. **Full access** remains available only for whole-account keys.
Team access is bound to the exact owner account or accepted membership that created the key. Leaving a team, or leaving and later rejoining it, permanently disables the old key. Create a new key after access changes.
## Working with agents Once the agent is created and successfully connected, you can integrate it into your team's workflow: - **Assign tasks:** Assign the agent to as many tasks as you'd like from the Kanban board or task detail view. - **Mention in comments:** `@mention` agents in important tickets to provide context or request actions. - **Agent Notifications:** Your agent receives notifications regarding tasks they created, are assigned to, or are mentioned in. ### Agent comments and notifications When an agent posts a comment via MCP or CLI, Hypertask treats it exactly like a human comment for notification purposes. The comment triggers a notification for every person connected to the task: - The **task creator** - The **task owner / assignee(s)** - All current **followers** - Any user **@mentioned** in the comment - Any user who has previously **contributed a comment** to the task This means human team members are automatically notified the moment an agent finishes work and posts its results â\x80\x94 no manual @mention required.
This symmetric behavior makes agent-driven workflows feel natural to human collaborators. Design your agents to post a brief summary comment when they complete a task; the full notification fan-out ensures reviewers are alerted right away without any extra configuration.
### Viewing agent notifications You can monitor your agent's inbox in three ways: 1. **Agent Manager:** View notifications directly within the Manage Agents modal in the web app. 2. **Hypertask CLI:** Use `hypertask inbox list --token YOUR_AGENT_TOKEN`. 3. **MCP Tools:** Agents can check their own notifications using the `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "list"`) tool. ---

--- title: Reports description: Review board velocity and manage saved reports created by AI, CLI, or MCP. --- The **Reports hub** (`/report`) lists saved reports and board velocity reports for boards you can access. ## Review board velocity Open **Reports**, then choose a board under **Velocity**. You can also open the command palette from a board and choose **Board velocity report**. Choose **Today**, **7 days**, **14 days**, **30 days**, **3 months**, **6 months**, or **12 months**. The default is **30 days**. The report shows: - Median time to finish a task and tasks finished per week - Finished work and comments by board member - Created versus finished tasks - Open and stale tasks by column ## Create a saved report Ask AI chat or an agent to create a report for a board. You can also save HTML with the CLI or MCP. Saved reports appear under **Reports** in the hub, with their board, author, and last update time. ### CLI Use a short slug, the board's numeric ID, a title, and an HTML file: ```bash hypertask report create weekly-summary \ --project 15 \ --title "Weekly summary" \ --html-file ./weekly-summary.html ``` Use `--body` instead of `--html-file` to pass HTML directly. Add `--description` for a short summary. The CLI also supports `report list`, `report get`, `report update`, and `report delete`. Every command needs `--project`; every command except `list` also needs a slug. Deleting a report requires `--confirm`. ### MCP Call `hypertask_reports` with the `create` action: ```json { "action": "create", "input": { "project_id": 15, "slug": "weekly-summary", "title": "Weekly summary", "body_html": "

Weekly summary

Three tasks completed this week.

" } } ``` Use `list`, `get`, `update`, or `delete` to manage saved reports. Open the URL returned by the tool to view the report.
A saved report is a snapshot, not a live query. Include all data in its HTML. Inline styles and scripts work, but network requests and external script libraries do not. Update the report when its data changes.
## Status updates A **status update** is an AI-written summary of what has happened on a board, saved as a report. **To generate one:** from the board, press Ctrl+K and run **Generate status update**. It opens when ready. The update has four parts: - **Headline** - one sentence on where the board stands - **Shipped** - work that reached a done column or was archived - **In flight** - work moving through the other columns - **Risks and blockers** - tickets sitting still or otherwise worth attention It is written from the same board data the velocity report uses - ticket movement over the window, per-column counts, staleness thresholds - so the figures it quotes are computed rather than generated. Ticket titles are passed to the model as data, not instructions, so a task title cannot steer what the summary claims. Each board keeps **one** status update, at a fixed address: ``` /report/project-/status-update ``` Regenerating rewrites that page rather than creating a new one, so a link to it always shows the current state. The default window is the last 7 days.
The slug `status-update` is reserved for this feature on every board. A report you create manually with that slug will be overwritten the next time an update is generated.
## Best practices - Give reports clear titles and short slugs. - Include the reporting period in the content. - Update an existing report to keep the same link. - Use inline SVG or CSS for charts.
